characterization: They cook most nights, one dish at a time, and they open two or three things before committing — the opening is browsing, not planning. Their real repertoire is four dishes: flattened quail, charred cabbage, long-cooked white beans, brothy beans and greens, all of which offer a choice of direction partway through. The declared dairy-free line doesn't hold up: they cook the brown-butter cabbage constantly, but bail out of cacio e pepe and anchovy butter at step one, every time, before touching a pan. What they're refusing isn't dairy, it's a dish where the dairy is the entire dish and there's nothing to decide. Chicken under a brick is the thing they keep opening and mostly don't make.
salientInference: Across the last ninety days, the dishes you return to over and over all branch partway through — you commit to recipes that leave a decision to you.

signals.rhythm: Nightly single-dish cooking, no batch day; browsing two or three options each evening and choosing late
